Fit indices of lavaan models

Source: R/gam.R, R/lavaan.R, R/meta.R, and 3 more
apa_performance.Rd

Fit indices of lavaan models

format model performance metrics in APA style

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gam'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("R2_adjusted", "Deviance_explained", "AIC"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bam'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("R2_adjusted", "Deviance_explained", "AIC"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lavaan'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("Chi2", "Chi2_df", "p_Chi2", "CFI", "TLI", "RMSEA", "RMSEA_CI", "SRMR"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'rma'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = NULL, column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'multinom'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'zeroinfl'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'hurdle'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "Sigma"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "Sigma"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'polr'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'clm'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = c("R2", "AIC"), column_formats = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'merMod'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("R2_marginal", "R2_conditional", "ICC"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'glmmTMB'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("R2_marginal", "R2_conditional", "ICC"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lme'
apa_performance(
  fit,
  metrics = c("R2_marginal", "R2_conditional", "ICC"),
  column_formats = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'list'
apa_performance(fit, metrics = NULL, column_formats = NULL)

Arguments

fit

model fit object

metrics

performance metrics. Default is R2 and Sigma

column_formats

column_formats object to format columns. If NULL, the default column_formats is used.

Value

tibble

Details

For generalized additive models (mgcv::gam and mgcv::bam), the metrics are the adjusted R^2^ ("R2_adjusted"), the percentage of the deviance explained ("Deviance_explained"), the number of observations ("n"), "AIC", and "BIC", as reported by summary(). The defaults are "R2_adjusted", "Deviance_explained", and "AIC".

For structural equation models and confirmatory factor analyses fit with lavaan (e.g., lavaan::cfa() or lavaan::sem()), the default metrics are the model \(\chi^2\) test ("Chi2", "Chi2_df", "p_Chi2"), the comparative fit index ("CFI"), the Tucker-Lewis index ("TLI"), the root mean square error of approximation with its confidence interval ("RMSEA", "RMSEA_CI"), and the standardized root mean square residual ("SRMR"). "AIC" and "BIC" are also available, and "all" selects every metric. Values come from lavaan::fitMeasures(). When the model was fit with a robust estimator (e.g., estimator = "MLR" or "WLSMV"), the scaled \(\chi^2\) test and the robust (or, if unavailable, scaled) CFI, TLI, and RMSEA are displayed. apa_note() gives the sample size, the estimator, and how missing data were handled, and defines the abbreviations.

For meta-analyses (metafor::rma()), the metrics are the number of studies ("k"), the test of residual heterogeneity ("QE" and "p_QE", with its df in the header), \(\tau^2\) ("tau2") and \(\tau\) ("tau"), \(I^2\) ("I2"), \(H^2\) ("H2"), confidence intervals of \(\tau^2\) and \(I^2\) ("tau2_CI" and "I2_CI", from stats::confint()), and, for meta-regressions, the omnibus test of the moderators ("QM" and "p_QM") and the proportion of heterogeneity they explain ("R2"). The defaults are "k", "QE", "p_QE", "tau2", and "I2", plus "QM", "p_QM", and "R2" for meta-regressions. Equal-effects models have no \(\tau^2\).

For multilevel meta-analyses (metafor::rma.mv()), "k" is the number of effect sizes, and the variance components are reported for each level: \(\sigma^2\) ("sigma2"), \(\sigma\) ("sigma"), and their confidence intervals ("sigma2_CI"), with the level as a subscript. "I2" is the multilevel \(I^2\) for all levels together, and "I2_levels" gives it for each level (Cheung, 2014). The defaults are "k", "QE", "p_QE", "sigma2", and "I2", plus "QM" and "p_QM" for meta-regressions.

For multinomial logistic regression models (nnet::multinom), R2 is McFadden's pseudo-R^2^, and the default metrics are R2 and AIC.

For zero-inflated and hurdle models (pscl::zeroinfl and pscl::hurdle), R2 is computed by performance::r2_zeroinflated(), and the default metrics are R2 and AIC.

For glm objects, R2 is the pseudo-R^2^ that performance::r2() selects for the model family (e.g., Tjur's R^2^ for logistic regression and Nagelkerke's R^2^ for count models). The header names the pseudo-R^2^ that was used. Because the residual standard deviation is not meaningful for most GLMs, the default metrics are R2 and AIC.

For mixed models (lme4::lmer, lme4::glmer, glmmTMB::glmmTMB, and nlme::lme), the default metrics are the marginal R^2^ (variance explained by the fixed effects), the conditional R^2^ (fixed and random effects), and the intraclass correlation (ICC), as computed by performance::model_performance().

For a list of models, each model's metrics are displayed in a row, labeled in a Model column by the list's names (or "Model 1", "Model 2", ... for unnamed elements). If metrics is NULL (default), each model's default metrics are used.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  model <- "visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
            textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
            speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9"
  fit_cfa <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939)
  apa_performance(fit_cfa)
}
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   `*&chi;*^2^` `*df*` `*p*` CFI   TLI   RMSEA `90% CI`   SRMR 
#>   <chr>        <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr>      <chr>
#> 1 85.31        24     <.001 .93   .90   .09   [.07, .11] .07  
# }
lm(mpg ~ cyl + wt, data = mtcars) |>
   apa_performance() |>
   apa_flextable()

R2
σe

list(
  `Cylinders` = lm(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars),
  `Cylinders and weight` = lm(mpg ~ cyl + wt, data = mtcars)
) |>
  apa_performance()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
